text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said on Tuesday it and the National Cancer Institute of the National Institutes of Health have agreed to continue their collaborative research on the development of Taxol.
They are continuing the cooperative research and development agreement through December 1997, Bristol-Myers Squibb said.
A second agreement was reached that would transfer exclusive rights to three National Cancer Institute inventions to Bristol-Myers Squibb for future development, the company said.

Bristol-Myers Squibb said it has agreed to provide the government with royalty and research support which will be used for important research projects at the National Cancer Institute and for additional TAXOL clinical trials.

The National Cancer Institute and Bristol-Myers Squibb collaborated in the development of TAXOL with the company, obtaining U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for the use of TAXOL in ovarian cancer at the end of 1992, the company said.
Since then, Bristol-Myers Squibb and the National Cancer Institute have sponsored an additional 500 clinical trials involving 25,000 patients, the company said.
The National Cancer Institute inventions granted to Bristol-Myers Squibb are for three treatment methods involving Taxol, a spokeswoman for the National Cancer Institute said.

The National Cancer Institute and Bristol-Myers Squibb are investing about $30 million a year, including the value of the Taxol that is supplied in the research, in the development of Taxol, the NCI spokeswoman said.
The royalty amount for the National Cancer Institute was not disclosed.
